$comment: The prestige case, and the building that closes a dead seam in this directory. `office-prestige` has been declared in data/traffic-profiles.json since Phase 1 and was used by NO shipped building -- a schema-valid profile reachable from nothing, which is exactly the shape DECISIONS.md SS D112 found in `destination-eta` and SS D114 in `measureEnergyLiveness`, one level up in data/. Invariant 7 makes strategy data; it does not make data exempt from having a caller. What the profile asks for is the opposite of Midtown Office: 16% of population per 5 min against 12, a 25 s target interval against 30, and a 20 s target wait against 25 -- a HARDER service level on a SMALLER population. So this building is deliberately not a big tower: 18 occupied floors at prestige density (34/floor, CIBSE Guide D 1 person per 12-15 m2 against a standard 1 per 8-10), 612 people, and six fast cars. The bank is oversupplied on purpose -- the interesting question at a headline address is not whether the lifts cope but whether a dispatcher can hold a 25 s interval when it has spare cars and a violent single-direction burst, which is where parking policy and pre-positioning are decided rather than capacity.
name: Chancery House
notes: Single bank, no zoning. At 18 floors a 5.0 m/s car reaches the top express in well under the time a second bank would save, and splitting six cars into two threes would halve the pooling benefit that makes the 25 s interval reachable at all. The building stresses stage 7 (repositioning) and stage 3 (scoring) rather than stage 2.

Cars are 2500 lb / 5.0 m/s gearless. CIBSE Guide D's code-minimum speed for a 76 m rise is well under this; the overspecification is the prestige brief and is the point -- it is what makes energy a live axis here, since a fast car that drives more to hold an interval spends more.
Population 612 over 18 floors. The whole building fits inside roughly four car-loads at 80% of rated capacity, so a single up-peak batch is a bank-scale event rather than a car-scale one.
